name: REP
desc: Integer bounds and aliases, all legal repetition counts and successor endpoints, finite and unbounded repetitions, zero-width and variable-width bodies, nested contexts, arrays and Unicode regexes, operand scope and evaluation, sequence-only restrictions, capture suppression and fresh function match states. Resource-counter details and optional fuzzy matching are outside these portable fixtures.

tests.name: Consuming bodies and continuation
tests.desc: Repetition counts body matches rather than consumed elements, retaining every legal endpoint for subsequent terms.

tests.name: Zero repetitions do not inspect an absent current element
Optional repetition retains its empty endpoint
Unbounded repetition retains shorter endpoints for continuation
Finite repetition retains every allowed endpoint
Repetition stops at the first incompatible element
Repeated adjacent pairs consume two elements per repetition
Repetition count is not the number of consumed elements
Partially matched body does not count as a repetition
Body ANY may consume different widths on different repetitions
Body ALL uses minimum coverage on every repetition
Nested repetition can split the consumed elements in several ways
Sibling repetitions resolve against the entire continuation
Repetition starts after a preceding sibling
Repetition can leave trailing input under HAS
Repeated array elements are atomic unless structurally matched
Repeated objects inherit exact matching mode
Repeated objects can explicitly request partial matching
Descending to a child array resets sequence context
Default one-element predicates cannot advance beyond the array end
Zero-width bodies and termination
tests.desc: Empty and mixed-width bodies can satisfy counts without progress. Unbounded repetition must terminate while preserving legal endpoints.

tests.name: Zero-width alternate-target assertions can repeat at array end
Zero-width body can satisfy a positive exact count
Zero-width negative assertions may be repeated without consumption
Failing zero-width body cannot satisfy a positive minimum
Empty alternatives can pad a count after consuming input
Unbounded mixed-width body terminates and retains all endpoints
Repetition of NONE EXISTS can assert an empty subject
Bound and body evaluation
tests.desc: Bounds evaluate once at the initial element; body expressions evaluate at successive positions. Constants and common expressions retain their contexts.

tests.name: Zero maximum aliases a nonzero computed minimum
Both bounds evaluate at the initial element rather than each iteration
Bounds may come from common value expressions
Body EXPR preserves sequence matching classification
REP itself may be supplied through an EXPR alias
NODE body patterns are evaluated at each successive element
Recoverable probes
tests.desc: Runtime INVALID_TARGET and INVALID_OPERAND faults are failed match probes. Static INVALID_GRAFT is permitted where specified, including unreachable syntax faults; intentional FAIL is not upgraded.

tests.name: Missing minimum reference is a failed probe
Missing maximum reference is a failed probe
Intentional bound failure remains a failed probe
Failed body probe stops repetitions but preserves earlier counts
Invalid REP operand is a false ANY child
Invalid bounds
tests.desc: Bounds must be integers, minimum must be nonnegative, and maximum must be -1, 0, or at least minimum.

tests.name: Syntax and sequence restrictions
tests.desc: SEQ may initiate sequence context only at the root of an array specification. Descending structurally starts ordinary element matching, while EXPR expansion preserves the declared expression classification. Runtime INVALID_TARGET and INVALID_OPERAND faults are failed match probes. Static INVALID_GRAFT is permitted where specified, including unreachable syntax faults; intentional FAIL is not upgraded.

tests.name: REP is illegal at the root of element matching
REP is illegal as an ordinary array element
REP does not become legal by nesting beneath ordinary ANY
REP is illegal in value context
REP legality is checked after EXPR expansion
Descending into an object resets REP legality
Unknown body expression is not a failed runtime probe
Zero count may skip body validation at runtime
Regex repetition and Unicode
tests.desc: Bodies may consume multiple codepoints or none. Continuation sees all endpoints, valid surrogate pairs remain intact, and supported lone surrogates remain individual codepoints.

tests.name: Counts characters rather than UTF-16 units
Exposes shorter choices to later literals
Regex empty literal repetitions are zero-width
Regex alternation between empty and nonempty literals terminates
Can begin after an unanchored search prefix
Cannot consume half a surrogate pair
Treats combining marks as separate codepoints
Regex zero-width alternate-target HAS can be repeated before a literal
Capture suppression
tests.desc: Named sequences below this operator do not produce captures or evaluate capture names, including in deeper arrays. SEQMIN/SEQMAX and CAP make results observable; CAPTURE starts an independent function match state where suppression no longer applies. Unrelated sibling captures remain visible.

tests.name: REP suppresses nested captures across repeated structural elements
REP does not evaluate unobservable capture names
REP suppressed names do not conflict between iterations
REP suppression stops at a fresh function match state
Data-derived bounds and boundary assertions
tests.desc: Invalid computed operands remain failed probes, and zero-width assertions can repeat at the start or end.

tests.name: Repetition minimum derived from the current data is a failed probe
Repetition maximum derived from data can be below the minimum
Data-derived invalid bounds remain recoverable inside NONE
Failed zero-width bound probe does not poison a later alternative
REP can repeat zero-width START before consuming data
REP can repeat zero-width END after consuming data
REP can combine zero-width body alternatives at the end
Unbounded repetition cannot recover after a mandatory body mismatch
Optional body with an intrinsically bad operand may be skipped
One-argument HAS and IS bodies
tests.desc: One-argument HAS/IS probes advance exactly one element regardless of child width; alternate-target forms are zero-width assertions and use ordinary matching for their alternate targets.

tests.name: One-argument HAS body counts repetitions separately from its lookahead width
One-argument IS body advances one after each sequence test
